en: Udāna 8.1 The First Discourse Connected with Nibbāna Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Blessed One was instructing, urging, rousing, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk concerning Nibbāna.
And those bhikkhus, having applied their whole minds and given full attention, were listening to the Dhamma with eager ears.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“There is, monks, that sphere where there is neither earth, nor water, nor fire, nor air;
neither the base of infinite space, nor the base of infinite consciousness, nor the base of nothingness, nor the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.”
"There is no this world, no other world, and no moon and sun.
In that regard, monks, I say there is neither coming nor going, nor standing still, nor passing away, nor being reborn;
it is without foundation, without occurrence, and entirely without an object."
“This, indeed, is the end of suffering. Thus [ends] the first [discourse].
